summary: Replaces the generated `sync` command at its registration site. internal/cli/root.go no longer calls rootCmd.AddCommand(newSyncCmd(flags)); it calls rootCmd.AddCommand(newGarminSyncStubCmd(flags)) instead -- one line, with a NOVEL comment naming this record. The stub (internal/cli/garmin_sync_stub.go) takes no flags of its own, prints "sync is superseded by history; run `garmin-pp-cli history`" to stderr and exits 2; under --json it writes exactly one line, {"event":"sync_superseded","hint":"garmin-pp-cli history","message":...}, to stdout and nothing to stderr. It sets SilenceErrors and SilenceUsage so its whole output is that one line whoever executes it, and it builds the exit-2 cliError directly rather than through usageErr, so the invocation journals as a runtime outcome rather than as a flag mistake the caller never made. GENERATED sync.go IS UNTOUCHED: newSyncCmd still compiles and is byte-identical to what the press emits; it is simply unreachable from the command tree. That is deliberate -- the press credits the sync FILE in its scorecard (scorecard.go:1531) and the live dogfood runs `sync` as a discarded pre-step (live_dogfood.go:810), so deleting the file would cost score for no behavioural gain, and a reprint would restore it anyway.
reason: N131 decision D11 (2026-09-13): `history` is the superset and `sync` is a dead end. The press emits `sync` with every SQLite store, and its walker knows three shapes -- page a flat list, add a `since=` filter the list endpoint declares, walk a parent table's rows into a child URL. Garmin's daily statistics are behind date-range endpoints whose URL carries the range and which refuse more than 28 days per call, or behind per-day endpoints answering for one date, so the calendar walk lives in `history`. Running one account through both verbs stored the activity feed and the per-activity heart-rate zones twice under different resource names, and re-paged the whole feed on every `sync`, because Garmin's activity list declares no filter the generator recognises. Once `history` gained activity detail, splits and the heart-rate-zone configuration (patch garmin-windowed-sync, same day), `sync` reached nothing `history` does not, and two verbs for one archive was a confusing surface on every press output -- CLI help, README, SKILL and the MCP mirror.
validated_outcome: gofmt -l clean, go vet clean, go build clean, go test -count=1 ./... green across 14 packages with 0 FAIL. Five tests (internal/cli/garmin_sync_stub_test.go): the command registered under `sync` lacks --resources, which the generated walker declares at internal/cli/sync.go:364, while a freshly built newSyncCmd still declares it -- so the marker is a real discriminator and the generated constructor is still compiled; no command anywhere in the tree carries the generated sync's flag pair, so the walker is unreachable; the text path writes exactly the one expected line to stderr and nothing to stdout and exits 2; the --json path writes exactly one parseable line carrying event=sync_superseded and a hint naming `history`, and nothing to stderr; and the superseded error is not classified by isCobraUsageError, so exit 2 here is not journalled as a usage failure. Probed on a rebuilt binary (2026-09-13, GARMIN_HOME pointed at a scratch home): `sync` printed the one line and exited 2; `sync --json` printed the one event line and exited 2. Press legs on this tree: verify 46/46 PASS with the `sync` row scoring 3/3 on the stub. NEW AND EXPECTED dogfood finding: "1 unregistered commands: sync" -- dogfood sees newSyncCmd defined and never registered, which is exactly this override; the verdict stays WARN, as it was before this patch.
regen_notes: A REPRINT REVERTS THIS: the generated root.go template emits rootCmd.AddCommand(newSyncCmd(flags)). After any reprint or regen-merge, replace that one line with rootCmd.AddCommand(newGarminSyncStubCmd(flags)) and restore the NOVEL comment above it. Nothing else in root.go changes, and internal/cli/sync.go must be left exactly as generated.

DO NOT DELETE THE GENERATED sync.go OR ITS TESTS. The scorecard credits the file's existence (scorecard.go:1531) and the live dogfood pre-step invokes the `sync` verb and discards the result (live_dogfood.go:810); the stub answers that invocation with exit 2, which the pre-step discards.

THE 12 GENERATED "run `garmin-pp-cli sync` first" HINTS STAY (analytics.go:47, data_source.go:243/341/725/728/754/783, doctor.go:678/711/754/760, search.go:141, plus the const in sync_hint.go). They lead to the stub, and the stub names `history`. Rewriting them would mean editing generated files a reprint restores, for a message that is already one hop from correct.

SPEC STRIP DONE, AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH: the 3 x-pp-sync-walker blocks are gone from spec.yaml, so the generated sync no longer walks activity detail, splits and hr zones per parent (sync.go loses its dependent-resource half, and store.go's resourceIDBaseOverrides, resourceParentKeyColumns and childScopeColumnSources go empty). The 17 x-pp-syncable markers stay and are inert either way: the extension is opt-IN and defaults to false (internal/openapi/parser.go sets endpoint.Syncable = pathSyncable || opSyncable), so `false` excludes nothing. The press still derives one syncable resource, `activities`, from the paginated activity-list endpoint, so this registration override remains the only thing making `sync` a dead end.

THE GENERATED MCP HINTS STAY TOO, SAME CLASS AS THE 12 CLI HINTS: internal/mcp/tools.go still tells an agent to run `sync` at :363 and :374 (the search and sql tool descriptions, 'Requires sync first.'), :849, :855 and :870 (the local-store error and next-step strings) and :1293 ('Run sync first to populate the local database.'). They are generated, a reprint restores them, and they lead to the stub, which names `history`. Only the two skew sentences were hand-edited: internal/mcp/tools.go:242 and :254, mirrored in tools-manifest.json:467 and :495. tools-manifest.json carries no other `sync` text.
